prompt.zh-TW: 現金流量允當比率想回答的是：本業賺進的現金，夠不夠支應哪三件事？
prompt.en: The cash flow adequacy ratio asks whether operating cash is enough to cover which three things?

text.zh-TW: 購置設備、增加存貨與發放現金股利
text.en: Buying equipment, building up inventory and paying cash dividends

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。這三項是公司維持與成長一定要用現金的地方，允當比率看本業的現金夠不夠支應。
feedback.en: That’s right. These three are the cash needs of keeping the business running and growing; the adequacy ratio asks whether operating cash covers them.

text.zh-TW: 償還借款、支付利息與繳納所得稅
text.en: Repaying loans, paying interest and paying income tax

feedback.zh-TW: 這些確實都要用現金，你的方向沒錯。不過利息與所得稅已經在營業活動的現金裡扣掉了，還款屬於籌資活動；允當比率的分母定義的是另外三項。
feedback.en: These do all use cash, so your thinking is on the right track. But interest and income tax are already deducted within operating cash, and loan repayments belong to financing; the adequacy denominator is defined as three other items.

text.zh-TW: 購買存貨、支付薪資與支付房租
text.en: Buying inventory, paying wages and paying rent

feedback.zh-TW: 存貨確實和分母有關，這點你想得沒錯。不過分母不是把整筆進貨放進去，只算本期存貨淨增加的部分（存貨增加額）；薪資與房租是日常營運支出，只會讓分子（營業活動的現金）變少，不在分母裡。允當比率的分母只有三項：資本支出、存貨增加額與現金股利。
feedback.en: You’re right that inventory matters here. But the denominator does not take every purchase, only the net increase in inventories for the period; wages and rent are day-to-day operating payments that only reduce the numerator (operating cash flow) and are not in the denominator. The denominator has just three items: capital expenditure, the increase in inventories and cash dividends.

explanation.zh-TW: {{term:tm_35qb8and}}的分母就是{{option:o_qa10}}，公式只指定這三項。{{option:o_ntjz}}裡的利息與稅屬於分子那一邊（已經在營業活動的現金裡扣掉），還款也不在這三項裡；{{option:o_qwpy}}裡的薪資與房租同樣只影響分子，進貨也不是整筆列入，只有存貨的淨增加（存貨增加額）才算進分母。
explanation.en: The denominator of the {{term:tm_35qb8and}} is exactly {{option:o_qa10}}; the formula names only these three. In {{option:o_ntjz}}, interest and tax sit on the numerator side (already deducted within operating cash) and loan repayments are not among the three items. In {{option:o_qwpy}}, wages and rent likewise only affect the numerator, and purchases do not go in whole: only the net increase in inventories enters the denominator.
